description: A formant voice after the IRCAM CHANT work: five parallel cells each firing short damped sine bursts at a formant frequency, with a slider that morphs the set through five vowels

params.text: Shifts that formant's frequency away from the vowel preset, an octave either way
Sets how wide that formant's resonance is, 30Hz to 500Hz
Sweeps the formant pattern through the vowels a, e, i, o and u, interpolating the first three formant frequencies between the presets
Sets how sharply each burst attacks, which sets the slope of the spectrum away from the formant
Chooses how a patched excitation is used: as audio put through a bank of resonant bandpass filters, or as triggers that each fire a fresh burst

inputs.text: Sets the pitch as a volt per octave with nothing patched at the excitation jack; with something patched there it transposes the whole formant pattern instead
The excitation source: patching it stops the internal oscillator and hands the module over to whichever mode the switch names
Shifts that formant's frequency, ±5V added to its offset knob
Changes that formant's bandwidth, ±5V added to its bandwidth knob
Moves the vowel morph, 0-10V across the whole sweep
Changes the attack sharpness, ±5V added to the skirt knob

notes: with nothing in the excitation jack the module is a voice of its own: an internal oscillator at the V/OCT pitch fires the bursts, and the mode switch does nothing
the per-formant frequency knobs are offsets on top of the vowel preset rather than absolute frequencies, so a vowel can be set and then one formant pushed away from it
